Wording is verbatim but the excerpt stops mid-sentence at 'the surviving parent takes half' and drops the rest of s.25, under which a surviving parent takes half and the brothers and sisters (including half-blood siblings related through the deceased parent) take the other half; s.25 is displaced here only on the researcher's unstated reading that Amali Perera's father died before her.

Excerpt and temporal note both check out: the corpus body is the consolidated text with latest_change_year 2024 and amendment events for 60-1947, 30-2022 and 4-2024, so the quoted wording cannot be shown to have been in force for the 2000 to 2015 deeds; correctly confined to background.
Confirmed: s.2(2) exists only in the post-2022 consolidated text, so it cannot govern the 2005 deed of gift; correctly recorded as unusable rather than relied on.
Verbatim; correctly recorded as an analogue that does not apply, the heirs in case 567/T being adults.

Cannot be checked from the corpus: the corpus carries the unamended s.8 consent wording with no amendment events and holds neither the Married Women's Property Ordinance No. 18 of 1923 nor any repealing instrument, so whether the husband's written consent was required in 2005 and 2013 is unresolvable here; note also that s.11, the District Court dispensation procedure, is the cross-referenced step the map does not record.

question_decisions.note: The pedigree and the fractions follow from ss.21, 22, 24, 26, 29 and 30, each checked verbatim, and the arithmetic reproduces: Kamal one half, three children one sixth each, Amali's one sixth splitting one twelfth to Anura Fernando and one twenty-fourth to each of Anusha and Anuk, plus Kamal's gift of one quarter to each, totalling eleven, eleven and two twenty-fourths. One claim, CL-M087-Q01-009, is rejected because the corpus nowhere states that title vests in the heirs at death and that an administrator's conveyance only records it; the fractions do not depend on it, so the question is left as proposed gold with that claim marked rejected.

The reservation is right and is now stronger than the researcher put it. Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 in the corpus is the post-2022 consolidation, with latest_change_year 2024 and amendment events 60-1947, 30-2022 and 4-2024, so neither s.2(1)(a) nor s.2(2)(b) can be shown to have governed the 2005, 2013 or 2015 deeds; Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.8 is unresolved on the corpus; and no corpus provision reaches acceptance of a gift by a minor donee or a reserved life interest.

Same chain as M087-Q01 carried through to fractions; all cited wording checked verbatim and the shares total twenty-four twenty-fourths. PROV-M087-001, s.21, moved from supporting to indispensable so the gateway provision carries the same role it has in M087-Q01; the hop count of four is unchanged because s.21 is already the first step of that chain.

disagreements.researcher_position: The answer is given for Lots 2 and 3 only, Lot 1 having been gifted away in 2005 and sold in 2013, with the alternative outcome for Lot 1 stated in the conclusion.
disagreements.verifier_position: The corpus holds nothing on reserved life interests, so which of Kanthi Perera and Amali Perera could have sold Lot 1 in 2013, and what passed by that sale, cannot be settled from statute; the alternative should be treated as live rather than as a footnote to a single gold answer.

disagreements.researcher_position: s.35 was considered and set aside because Lot 1 was gifted subject to a life interest and had left the estate, and the questions ask only for the pedigree and the present shares.
disagreements.verifier_position: s.35 is in the corpus, was checked and is at least arguable: Amali Perera received Lot 1 from her mother in 2005 and became an heir to the same parent in 2014, which is the situation the section addresses, and if collation applied the children's shares would not be equal.

unsupported_claims: CL-M087-Q01-009 rejected. It asserts that the Administrator's Conveyance of 3rd December 2015 records a devolution that had already taken effect by operation of law at the death, citing PROV-M087-001, s.21. Section 21 says only which law governs inheritance. Searches across the Civil Procedure Code testamentary chapter, ss.526, 528, 541, 542, 554A and 737, found nothing stating when title vests in the heirs, so the proposition is Roman-Dutch or practice authority, not corpus statute.

CL-M087-Q02-001 marked disputed. It states that every disposition in the pedigree had to be by a notarially attested deed and cites PROV-M087-011, whose wording is the post-2022 consolidation of Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2. The proposition is almost certainly right historically but cannot be shown from the frozen corpus for deeds of 2000, 2005, 2013 and 2015.
temporal_issues: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2, PROV-M087-011 and PROV-M087-012: the corpus shows in_force_from_year 1840, latest_change_year 2024 and amendment events 60-1947 s.2, 30-2022 s.2 and 4-2024 s.2. The researcher's treatment is confirmed; neither entry may be relied on for any deed in the scenario, and PROV-M087-012, the guardian for a minor transferee, post-dates the 2005 gift by seventeen years.

Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.8, PROV-M087-016: the corpus shows no amendment events at all, so it cannot show whether the husband's-consent requirement stood in 2005 and 2013. Set to unresolved rather than left as an inapplicable proposal.

Sections 2, 20 to 32, 35 and 36 of 15-1876 all show in_force_from_year 1876 and no latest_change_year, so the Part III chain is temporally clean for the 2014 deaths and for the April 2019 reference date.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: 15-1876/s3 defines 'immovable property' and the corpus graph records s.21 as pointing to it. The definition is satisfied on these facts, land in Colombo, but the map does not record it.

15-1876/s11, the District Court order dispensing with the husband's consent, is the procedure that goes with s.8. If the s.8 consent requirement is held to have survived, s.11 and not s.8 alone is the step that answers M087-Q02, and the map does not record it.

15-1876/s35, collation, is in the corpus and bears on the equality of the children's shares after the 2005 gift; the researcher's rejection is reasoned but is a judgment call, recorded above as a disagreement.

2-1889/s541(c), which forbids an administrator appointed pendente lite from executing a deed of conveyance of immovable property before confirmation of sale, is the closest limit in the corpus on an administrator's power to convey and is not recorded; it does not answer the termination point either.

The Partition Law No. 21 of 1977 is not in the corpus, so the conclusiveness of the Final Decree of 2nd December 1999, the root of Kanthi Perera's title to Lot 3, has no statutory support in the map. This gap is not listed in corpus_gaps.
case_law_dependence: M087-Q01 and M087-Q03 remain answerable from statute for the fractions. The only Roman-Dutch or case-law dependence inside them is the vesting-at-death proposition in CL-M087-Q01-009, now rejected, and the life-interest point, which both answers keep outside the fractions.

M087-Q02 is correctly reserved: acceptance of a gift for a minor donee and the effect of a reserved life interest both fall to Roman-Dutch law through 15-1876/s36, and the age of majority is fixed in the corpus only by 2-1889/s502, which is expressly limited to that Chapter.
enrichment_issues: No enrichment applied to any of the three questions; all three are 'keep' questions in the candidate file, so enrichment.applied false is correct. No statute name, section number or conclusion is leaked into any background text.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: PROV-M087-011 and PROV-M087-012 are two entries on the same section_id 7-1840/s2 with different subsections. This is not a duplicate on the schema, which keys on provision_id, but a reader comparing section ids will see the same section twice with different temporal treatment.
The three gold answers name no case, report series or judge; the validator's case-law check is clean.

lawyer_questions: Does 'after her marriage to Anura Fernando he passed away' refer to Amali Perera's father, as the whole gold answer assumes, or to Anura Fernando? If Anura predeceased Amali there is no surviving spouse under s.22 and her one sixth goes wholly to Anusha and Anuk, changing every fraction in M087-Q01 and M087-Q03. The candidate file already flags this sentence as having ambiguous pronouns.
Is it safe to read the scenario as putting Amali Perera's father's death before her own? If he survived her, s.25 and not s.26 governs and he would take half of her one twelfth.

Did the Married Women's Property Ordinance No. 18 of 1923 remove the husband's-consent requirement in 15-1876/s8? If it did, PROV-M087-016 should be dropped rather than carried as unresolved, and one of the two instances sought by M087-Q02 disappears.
Should collation under 15-1876/s35 have been applied to the 2005 gift of Lot 1 to Amali Perera when the children took their shares in 2014?
Could an administrator validly execute a conveyance on 3rd December 2015 after the proceedings in DC Colombo 567/T were terminated on 6th November 2015? Nothing in the corpus answers this.
